chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of his companions, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When the belly is satiated, it rebels.

key_terms.الْبَطْنُ: The belly/stomach, representing physical appetite and consumption
key_terms.طَغَى: Rebelled, became arrogant, or exceeded limits, indicating spiritual deviation

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual effect of overeating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni places this concise narration of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) within the chapter on 'Abhorrence of abundant eating,' reflecting the Shia emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) as a means to purify the soul. The term *tagha* (transgression/arrogance) implies that physical satiety dulls spiritual vigilance, leading the individual to exceed moral boundaries and disobey divine commands. This hadith serves as a foundational principle in Shia ethical scholarship, linking bodily discipline directly to spiritual clarity and obedience.
